Thanks — we can provide everything you asked for. I'm attaching an initial SCIM attribute mapping (legend_med_scim_mapping_v1.csv) and a redacted SAML assertion sample (saml-assertion-sample.xml) to start. Quick summary here, and Marissa will follow up with technical details and sync timing. Naomi is cc'd for any compliance evidence requests (SOC2, audit logs).

High-level answers:
- SCIM: Redwood implements SCIM 2.0; we support PATCH (RFC 7644), full PUT, and bulk operations for onboarding. We also support incremental fetches via standard filtering on meta.lastModified (e.g., filter=meta.lastModified gt "2027-04-18T00:00:00Z").
- Conflict resolution: externalId is the canonical identifier if provided. If absent, we match on primary email; duplicates trigger a conflict flag in the provisioning logs and are surfaced in the Console with the proposed merge options.
- Group sync: group membership can be synced to map to RBAC roles. You can set precedence rules per mapping (e.g., most-permissive or most-restrictive).
- SAML/OIDC: we accept transient or persistent NameID; recommended attributes include email, given_name, family_name, and a groups attribute (or redwood_roles). Session lifetime is configurable per SP connection; we enforce token/SSO session timeouts server-side with optional session revocation on logout. OIDC supported for customers who prefer JWT-centric flows.

Next steps: Marissa — can you add the SCIM handling details (sync cadence, PATCH handling examples, provisioning error payloads) and a short checklist for the staged test? Naomi — I'll put the SOC2 link and audit-log retention details in a follow-up.

Hi Emily —

Quick technical follow-up with specifics you can include in your RFP response. I'm keeping examples concise so you can paste into Jira or your procurement doc.

SCIM specifics (Redwood behavior):
- Version: SCIM 2.0 (RFC 7643/7644)
- Supported operations: POST (create), GET (read), PUT (replace), PATCH (modify), DELETE. Bulk operations supported for initial onboarding (we recommend batching <= 2,000 records per bulk request).
- Incremental sync: we support filtering on meta.lastModified and the RFC filter parameter (e.g., GET /Users?filter=meta.lastModified+gt+2027-04-18T00:00:00Z). For very large directories, we offer a paged delta endpoint in Dedicated/Private deployments (uses opaque checkpoint tokens).
- Conflict policy: when externalId is supplied in the SCIM payload we treat it as the authoritative mapping. If externalId is not provided, we match on primaryEmail (case-insensitive). On duplicates we: 1) mark the user as conflicted in the provisioning log, 2) attempt no-merge automated rules (do not assume merge), and 3) surface an action in Console for admin to resolve. Logging includes the original payload and suggested resolution.
- Group sync: groups are treated as first-class resources. You can map scim groups -> role_id in Redwood. Role precedence is configurable (choose most-restrictive by default for safety).
- Attribute mapping: we support standard SCIM schemas plus extension attributes. Example mapping columns are in the CSV attached (externalId, userName, name.givenName, name.familyName, emails[type=work].value, active, groups).
- Rate/latency guidance: for Hosted customers we recommend 5-30s group sync cadence for active directories; Dedicated/Private can push to 5s intervals. For very large directories we recommend an initial bulk followed by incremental PATCH/GET syncs.

SAML/OIDC specifics:
- NameID formats: persistent or emailAddress (we recommend persistent for security).
- Required attributes we recommend: email (urn:oid:0.9.2342.19200300.100.1.3), given_name, family_name, groups (as a multi-valued attribute or roles claim).
- Session lifetime: default SSO session is 8 hours; we honor SP-initiated sessionMax settings and we support per-realm overrides. Token TTLs for OIDC id_tokens are configurable.
- Logout: support for SAML SingleLogout (SLO) and OIDC back-channel logout in Dedicated/Private. Hosted supports front-channel logout and optional back-channel with enterprise customers.

Admin & RBAC controls:
- Default roles: Organization Admin (full), App Admin (manage apps & routes), Security Auditor (read-only access to logs & policies), Billing (billing & subscription), Support (limited troubleshooting).
- Custom roles: yes — you can create custom roles and bind them to groups via Console or SCIM group-to-role mapping. Custom roles support fine-grained permissions (e.g., can_create_models=false, can_deploy=false).
- Delegated admin: scope down by org unit, cloud region, or product area. Delegated admins get scoped tokens with limited console visibility and enforced MFA for elevated actions.
- Approval/workflow: role elevation can be gated by an approval workflow (email or Slack webhook) and logs are recorded as immutable audit events.

Provisioning error payloads & observability:
- Errors: we return detailed SCIM error objects with error code, scimType, and diagnostic message.
- Audit logs: provisioning requests, conflicts, and admin resolves are recorded for 365 days by default for Hosted; retention options extendable for Dedicated/Private.

Staged test checklist (recommended):
1) Create test SP/IDP config in test tenant.
2) Push 10 test users + 1 group via bulk SCIM POST.
3) Verify group->role mapping and sign-in via SAML.
4) Test PATCH updates (change department, email alias).
5) Introduce duplicate primaryEmail to validate conflict handling.
6) Review provisioning logs and resolve conflict via Console (admin action).

I'll attach a short packet (redwood_scim-overview.pdf) with examples and a sample curl sequence for PATCH operations. If it helps, we can do a 30min smoke session to walk your infra team through the test.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Identity & Integrations
Redwood Inference

Hi Emily —

Answers inline: 

1) Opaque checkpoint tokens: Currently Hosted customers can use timestamp-based incremental filtering (meta.lastModified). The opaque checkpoint token (fast delta with server-side checkpoints) is available for Dedicated and Private deployments. For large directories we recommend Dedicated or a hybrid where you run an initial bulk via Dedicated then continue incremental via Hosted filters for day-to-day deltas.

2) Automated merge rules: yes — Console supports configurable conflict resolution policies. Default is no-auto-merge; you can enable safe-auto-merge rules such as exact email alias match + exact name match. We keep a pre-merge audit trail and require a separate admin flag to enable any auto-merge policy.

3) Minimal PATCH example (SCIM v2):
PATCH /Users/2819c223-7f76-453a-919d-0f276bb6f0d1
Content-Type: application/scim+json

{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    {"op": "Replace", "path": "groups", "value": [{"value": "group-hr-234"}]},
    {"op": "Replace", "path": "active", "value": false}
  ]
}

SOC2 & audit logs: Naomi — can you drop the public SOC2 statement link and our standard retention table into the Drive folder? Naomi Feldman is on this thread and will post the cert link (we host certs in our customer portal).

Next tactical: please pick a 30-minute slot for Apr 26-28 for the smoke test. We will provision a test tenant and a canary group for you. After the test we can run a short postmortem and provide the final evidence package with logs and sample error records.
